title: The Cover of Tashkent
premise: Gideon Thornbury, a veteran air-crash investigator haunted by the row-twelve deaths of his wife and daughter, is approached by a stranger named Mara Voss who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of. She repays it by pulling him into a covert network planning an aviation 'accident' designed to conceal a political assassination, and Gideon realizes his own rewritten incident reports were used to build the cover story. As he races to expose the scheme, he must choose between protecting his found family of fellow investigators and telling a truth that will destroy the institution that gave his grief meaning. In the end, Gideon grounds the flight and testifies at cost to everything but himself, finding that memory — even painful memory — is the only loyalty worth keeping.
about_author: Orsen Nakamura is a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. He lives between Tashkent and Lisbon, writing thrillers about systems, grief, and the people who keep both running.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Twelve years after losing his family in Flight 4471's crash, Gideon works a routine investigation in Tashkent, rigidly procedural, emotionally sealed. A young colleague, Dara, cracks his armor slightly. Emotional beat: grief as routine, the ache beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Mara Voss appears at his hotel bar, thanking him for saving her in Almaty years ago — an event Gideon cannot recall. She leaves a keycard and a warning: 'They're rewriting you.' POV: Gideon. Beat: uncanny disruption of his ordered world.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We learn she was a logistics operative inside Meridian Group, a private risk firm, and that Gideon's old reports were altered to pre-clear a future 'accident.' She owes him a debt she invented to reach him. Beat: guilt disguised as gratitude.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Report
chapters.summary: Gideon pulls his archived findings on Flight 4471 and finds digital fingerprints of tampering — his conclusions softened, causes reassigned. POV: Gideon. Beat: the ground tilts; his life's careful rules were built on edited sand.

chapters.title: Dara
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The junior investigator notices Gideon unraveling and covers for him with their supervisor, revealing her own history: her brother died in a crash officially ruled pilot error. Beat: the first bond of found family forms over shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Mara walks Gideon through Meridian Group's structure — shell companies, insurance arbitrage, a standing capability to stage disasters. POV alternates via debrief scene. Beat: horror of scale; the accident is a product line.

chapters.title: The Passenger List
chapters.summary: Gideon identifies the target: reformist minister Anvar Rahimov, booked on Flight 772 from Tashkent in eleven days, seated — deliberately — in row twelve. POV: Gideon. Beat: cold recognition; they chose his row on purpose.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: Gideon confronts his old mentor, Director Hale, who warns him off with veiled threats and hints that compliance once saved Gideon's career. POV: Gideon. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its real war.

chapters.title: Almaty, Remembered Wrong
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter, Gideon's fragmented memory of the Almaty layover where he may have pulled a woman from a collapsing terminal — or dreamed it. Mara confirms details only a witness would know. Beat: memory as unreliable currency.

chapters.title: The Cell
chapters.summary: Mara reintroduces her former team: Kessler the engineer, Ilya the fixer, and the cold planner called Only. Gideon attends a briefing undercover. POV: Gideon. Beat: walking into the machine, heart hammering under a borrowed face.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Gideon tries to flag Flight 772 through official channels and is stonewalled — his access revoked, his file flagged for 'psychological review.' POV: Dara. Beat: institutions close ranks; the system protects itself, not the dead.

chapters.title: What Dara Found
chapters.summary: Dara independently traces maintenance records showing a component swap scheduled on 772 — matching Meridian's signature. She brings it to Gideon unasked. Beat: trust deepens into partnership; two broken investigators become a unit.

chapters.title: Only
chapters.summary: Only's POV. The planner senses a leak, tests Mara with a false detail, and begins closing the net. Cold, methodical menace. Beat: the hunter turns; clock accelerates.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: Meridian's cleaners hit Mara's safehouse; Gideon and Dara extract her through Tashkent's night markets. Ilya dies covering them. POV: Gideon. Beat: first blood, first irreversible choice.

chapters.title: Confession at Altitude
chapters.summary: Mara confesses the favor was manufactured — she never met Gideon before; she studied his file and built a debt he'd believe. POV: Mara. Beat: betrayal and strange relief; the lie was the truest thing offered to him.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon breaks into Hale's archive and finds twelve years of adjusted reports — including the one that buried the true cause of Flight 4471: a Meridian-linked sensor fault. Beat: devastating revelation; his family's death was part of the pattern.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: With three days to departure, the trio plans to ground 772 without tipping Meridian: a whistleblower filing, a maintenance hold, a press failsafe. POV rotates. Beat: purpose crystallizes; fear becomes fuel.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Kessler, uneasy about staging a crash, defects to Gideon with the device schematics — but Only anticipated it, feeding him a decoy. POV: Kessler. Beat: hope laced with trap.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Again
chapters.summary: At the airport, Gideon boards 772 during pre-flight to physically verify the tampered component, nearly caught by Only's man. He finds the real fault exactly where his daughter would have sat. Beat: climax approaches; the past literally in his hands.

chapters.title: Grounding 772
chapters.summary: Climax. Using Kessler's evidence and Dara's records, Gideon forces an emergency airworthiness directive minutes before departure; Only tries to trigger the device remotely and is stopped when Mara sacrifices her escape to jam the uplink. Only is arrested; the flight lands empty of catastrophe. Beat: victory purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Gideon testifies publicly, burning his career and naming Hale, who resigns rather than face trial. The truth about Flight 4471 finally enters the record. POV: Gideon. Beat: loyalty to the dead fulfilled through truth, not silence.

chapters.title: The Cover of Tashkent
chapters.summary: Months later, Gideon, Dara, and Mara share tea above the city — an unlikely family forged in lies and kept by honesty. Gideon finally remembers Almaty clearly: there was no rescue; Mara simply saw a man who needed a reason. Beat: quiet resolution; found family, chosen truth.
